correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and zero-target normalization are explicit. Injective edge-weight-to-Laplacian map and strict trace-inverse convexity prove unrestricted uniqueness under graph automorphism averaging. The symmetric/antisymmetric spectra yield the exact rational objective. For m>=3, three strictly positive directional derivatives, verified by coefficientwise positivity in h=m-3, establish the zero-central-edge optimal point. For m=2 the exact Kemeny objective on the zero-holding curve has a unique cubic critical point, and the other two KKT derivatives are strictly positive. Full matrix and symbolic verifier replay passed 28 direct exact test cases. Finite tests are corroboration, not proof of infinite result.

originality.rationale: The earlier October 2026 same-graph SLEM theorem already establishes the bridge-deletion boundary at three pages: it is expressly excluded from the novelty claim in isolation. The new, strictly convex Kemeny inverse-gap objective yields a unique all-size optimizer and minimum, and every such optimizer has SLEM one, while the earlier fastest-mixing optimum has SLEM strictly smaller than one. For m>=3 the exact peripheral-rung allocation lies outside the recorded SLEM-optimal interval. value.rationale: An infinite natural graph family exhibits a precise edge-suppression boundary when the page count reaches three; unlike a routine graph invariant computation, this classifies the unrestricted edge probability design uniquely. The optimum remains irreducible but becomes periodic, separating minimization of stationary-target hitting time from actual mixing. A natural maximum-degree Markov walk suffers an exact asymptotic factor of 4/3, establishing a quantified design consequence.
